---
title: "Hands-on Exercise 5"
subtitle: "Second-order Spatial Point Patterns Analysis"
---

This exercise examines whether point events interact across a range of distances and whether the observed pattern is more clustered or dispersed than an appropriate reference process.

::: {.chapter-link}
[Open the course reference for Chapter 5](https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap05.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

## Learning focus

- Prepare spatial point-pattern data and a valid observation window.
- Use the G-function to study nearest-event distances.
- Use the F-function to study empty-space distances.
- Use K- and L-functions to assess spatial dependence across distances.
- Compare observed statistics with simulation envelopes.

## Analysis workflow

1. Import and validate the study-area and event data.
2. Convert the data into the structures required for point-pattern analysis.
3. Define a suitable null model and simulation settings.
4. Compute G-, F-, K-, and L-function diagnostics.
5. Interpret departures from the simulation envelope carefully and in context.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Conclusions depend on the observation window, edge correction, distance range, and reference process used.
:::
